A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiffusionDrive work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. The supplied v1 ends after its references; v2 adds Supplementary Material A–C. The available material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Tables 1–7 report original DiffusionDrive evaluations on NAVSIM and nuScenes, including component ablations and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds driving-prior ablations, CARLA evaluations and qualitative examples in the supplement.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the anchored Gaussian initialization, truncated diffusion schedule, cascade decoder, training loss and inference procedure. Appendix B tests alternative priors as ablations without revising the proposed method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates NAVSIM and nuScenes. Appendix B adds CARLA training and Longest6 evaluation using NAVSIM-derived anchors, extending coverage to a distinct simulator domain and testing transfer of the anchor source.

E2.justification: Table 8 adds current-status extrapolated trajectories as alternative driving priors, using both inference-only substitution and a trained single-anchor variant. The comparator sets in Tables 1–7 remain unchanged; CARLA reuses Transfuser as its comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds CARLA Longest6 evaluation with DS, RC and IS metrics, plus controlled training/inference prior substitutions. Existing main evaluation settings are retained. Appendix A reports ImageNet initialization alongside retained 'from scratch' wording, leaving any actual initialization change unresolved.

E4.justification: Appendix B newly tests whether clustered anchors outperform extrapolated priors and whether NAVSIM anchors transfer to CARLA. Appendix C adds nine qualitative cases covering straight driving, left turns and right turns, substantially extending the original analyses.

E5.justification: Table 9 introduces ± uncertainty reporting for CARLA DS, RC and IS, absent from v1's results. The PDFs do not specify the uncertainty statistic, run count or seeds, so additional repeated runs cannot be established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical values. New Table 8 reports PDMS 81.3 and 84.7 for extrapolated-prior variants versus the retained 88.1 baseline. Table 9 adds CARLA DS 64.27 ± 2.43, compared with a cited Transfuser result of 47.30 ± 5.72. Added qualitative findings include stopping at a traffic light and overtaking.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, including the diffusion formulation, mode-diversity definition and loss, are unchanged. The supplement introduces no proofs or new formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same method and central claims: diverse driving trajectories, a tenfold reduction in denoising steps, 88.1 NAVSIM PDMS and 45 FPS.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly attributes extrapolated priors' weaker performance to insufficient action-space coverage. It also interprets the CARLA results as evidence that anchors generalize across datasets rather than exploiting training/validation information leakage.

D1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands training documentation: ImageNet initialization, 32 m LiDAR extent, auxiliary perception tasks, and nuScenes training using an official stage-1 checkpoint followed by 10 stage-2 epochs. These important reproduction details were absent from the supplied v1; the code/model/demo link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds image-generation diffusion literature, including DDPM, flow matching and TDPM, distinguishing explicit driving priors from implicit intermediate distributions. The dedicated VBD explanation is removed, although that work remains cited.

P1.justification: The main section structure and most prose are retained, with localized tightening of explanations. A related-work paragraph and Supplementary Material A–C organize the additions without a broad narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8–9 and three full-page qualitative figures, Figures 5–7, containing nine additional case panels. Existing main figures and tables remain, with limited resizing, caption editing and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The new prior ablations and CARLA anchor-transfer test strengthen validation of the retained method, while Appendix A and the TDPM discussion improve reproducibility information and research positioning. The gains are limited by sparse CARLA protocol documentation, undefined uncertainty reporting, and unreconciled ImageNet initialization versus 'from scratch' wording.
